subject: Service fallthrough credit carveout request
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@octaviahealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Octavia Procurement <procurement@octaviahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for planned maintenance windows and monthly credit structure

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the run-through last week. To move forward we need to reconcile two items with our procurement team:

1) Octavia has a number of quarterly maintenance events (hardware refresh and on-site validation) that can lead to short regional unavailability. Historically our platform vendors have accepted a limited "planned maintenance" carveout to uptime calculations, and we want to propose the following: exclude up to 12 cumulative hours per month of scheduled maintenance from the uptime denominator for the US-west region if notified 10 days in advance.

2) For unplanned outages that exceed 30 minutes per day in aggregate, procurement requests a monthly service credit structure that scales: 2% credit for 99.5-99.0% effective availability, 5% for 99.0-98.0%, and 12% for <98.0%.

We attached our suggested SLA addendum and a calendar of planned maintenance windows for Q4. Can Redwood accept carved-out maintenance hours with a notification timeframe and the stepped monthly credit table above? If not, what alternatives could we offer to reach commercial consensus quickly?

Appreciate your help—procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Director, IT Vendor Management
Octavia Health
Attachment: Octavia_SLA_Request_v3.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@octaviahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for planned maintenance windows and monthly credit structure

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear request and the calendar. High level: Redwood can support a bounded planned-maintenance carveout, but we need to align on notification windows, operational controls (which jobs get drained / KV cache invalidation), and an upper bound on cumulative monthly carveouts so platform SLAs remain meaningful for other tenants.

A few proposals from our side:
- We can accept up to 8 cumulative hours/month excluded from the uptime denominator for scheduled maintenance per region with a 7-business-day notice.
- If you require 12 hours/month, we can accommodate but only with a compensating commitment: predictable maintenance windows (published quarter ahead) plus a dedicated maintenance routing policy to isolate Octavia traffic during those windows. That would be part of a Dedicated plan amendment.
- For credit tiers: your stepped table is reasonable, but we prefer to cap the maximum monthly credit at 10% for availability <98% in hosted mode; higher caps are available under Dedicated/Private contracts.

I've looped in Marissa for commercial sizing and Laura for legal redlines. Vivek can comment on operational feasibility (cache/eviction and KV replication impact). Can we sync Wed 30th at 10am PT for a short call?

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: carveout for planned maintenance windows and monthly credit structure

Folks —

Quick notes after talking to Rishi pre-call:
- Octavia is enterprise (healthcare), high-value ARR, looking to close Dedicated commitment if commercial terms allow the maintenance carveout they want.
- They are sensitive to operations during on-site refreshes (they prefer regional blackout periods vs rolling maintenance).

Vivek, two asks for the call: can you summarize the technical controls we'd need to safely exclude scheduled maintenance from uptime metrics (drain strategy, KV cache dump, warmup time estimate)? Also estimate the additional ops cost of a dedicated maintenance routing policy.

Laura, I'd like a quick read on whether a 12-hour carveout + 10% cap is something we can propose in a redline or if we should counter with 8 hours + 10% max unless they move to Dedicated.

Thanks — Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for planned maintenance windows and monthly credit structure

Marissa —

Legal redline summary and negotiating position:
- We can agree to a planned-maintenance carveout, but propose 8 hours/month excluded with 7-business-day notice. The rationale is preserving SLA integrity across shared tenancy.
- For the credit table, accept the tiered approach but cap credits at 10% for the lowest band in hosted. We should also add a clause that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability breaches (standard limitation language).
- If Octavia requires 12 hours/month excluded OR a higher credit cap, recommend we move them to a Dedicated contract where we can offer more flexible credits and scheduled blackout windows under a higher recurring commitment.

I've prepared a redline (attached) that includes the carveout definition (what counts as scheduled maintenance), notice requirements, and a requirement that scheduled maintenance must be listed on Octavia's published maintenance calendar and mutually agreed each quarter. Also added an operational runbook appendix to reduce risk.

Attachment: redwood_response_draft.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@octaviahealth.com>, Octavia Procurement <procurement@octaviahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for planned maintenance windows and monthly credit structure

Alicia —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of our proposed compromise (attached redline):

- Planned maintenance carveout: Redwood will exclude up to 8 cumulative hours/month, per-region, from the uptime denominator for scheduled maintenance provided Octavia publishes the windows at least 7 business days in advance and updates the shared maintenance calendar each quarter.
- If Octavia requires a 12-hour/month carveout, Redwood can support that under a Dedicated commitment. We can draft a Dedicated addendum outlining routing isolation and warmup expectations.
- Monthly credit structure: we accept the stepped table concept but propose the following hosted caps: 2% for 99.5-99.0%, 5% for 99.0-98.0%, and 10% for <98.0% (max). Credits are calculated on monthly invoice and are the exclusive remedy for availability breaches.
- Operational mitigations: we will provide an operational runbook for maintenance windows (drain process, cache snapshot/restore steps, expected warmup latency) and a dedicated escalation contact during maintenance.

Next steps: please confirm if Octavia can accept the 8-hour carveout + credit caps for hosted, or if you prefer to discuss Dedicated terms for the 12-hour ask. If acceptable, we will circulate a redlined SLA addendum and a DocuSign for signature.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_response_draft.docx, Octavia_maintenance_calendar.csv
